overview:
The **Battle of Nal Hutta (Great War)** (3640 BBY) was a pivotal engagement of the **Great War (SWTOR)**, fought on or above **Nal Hutta**. Hutt cartel mercenaries fighting alongside sith imperial units in nal hutta swamp palace districts during a republic raid.

Archives record this battle across saga films, animated series, Knights of the Old Republic, Old Sith Empire chronicles, and expanded universe sources — anchoring the Great War (SWTOR) in both cinematic canon and deep galactic history.
history:
Military historians of the New Republic classify the Battle of Nal Hutta (Great War) within the broader **Great War (SWTOR)** campaign. Front-line reports describe hutt cartel mercenaries fighting alongside sith imperial units in nal hutta swamp palace districts during a republic raid.

Commanders on both sides leveraged local terrain, orbital support, and Force-sensitive operatives where available. The engagement's outcome shifted regional control and fed into later battles documented across the same war.

For chronology enthusiasts, **3640 BBY** places this conflict in the galactic timeline alongside other famous battles of the Great War (SWTOR).
significance: The Battle of Nal Hutta (Great War) illustrates how the Great War (SWTOR) reshaped the galaxy — through combined arms warfare, political betrayal, and the eternal struggle between light and dark. Its legacy persists in memorials, veteran accounts, and holodramas spanning nine saga films and decades of tie-in fiction.
